newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed on Monday, although some traders said the market could ease in line with losses in London overnight.
London robusta futures were weaker at midday on Monday, but off earlier lows. At the break, September was down $11, to $1,607, after ranging from $1,611 to $1,585. November sagged $4, to $1,606.

On Friday, New York arabica futures ended mixed in uneventful, thin trading. September rose 0.45 cent per lb firmer, at 184.95 cents, after ranging from 187.00 to 183.25 cents. Second-month December fell 0.25 cent, to 162.30 cents, while the back months closed down 0.25 to 1.05 cents.
The September/December switch widened to 22.65 cents compared with 21.95 cents at the close on Thursday.
Technically, traders pegged September support at 181.50-180.00 cents, followed by 178.00 cents. On the upside, they said resistance was seen near 190.00 cents.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Monday that no damaging cold weather is in sight for Brazil's coffee belt during the next five days. Some cooler conditions may develop during the middle of next week, WSC said, but no damaging cold is indicated.
After Friday's close the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 3,092 60-kg bags as of July 31, to 95,491 bags. An additional 250 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

Also after Friday's close, the CFTC Commitment of Traders report showed non-commercial long positions increased by 120 lots in the two weeks ended July 29, to 3,294 lots. Non-commercial short positions decreased by 347 lots, to 1,289 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks fell by 249 lots, to 8,169 lots and commercial short positions rose by 1,806 lots, to 12,621 lots.
Nonreportable long positions increased by 1,243 lots, to 9,606 lots, while nonreportable short positions decreased by 345 lots, to 7,159 lots.
